state.product: Can targets economical AI-generated CRUD SaaS. Prioritize adoption, compact unambiguous source, source-owned reusable composition, one canonical primitive, total maintenance. Runtime permissions, actual caller, declaration identity, failure/order/atomicity and recovery may not be weakened. Both choices leave .can syntax and author token count unchanged; generated output and implementation costs can differ.
state.actual_failure: Original selected CanCRM promotion schemas/policies + unchanged saved Given emit successfully via real CLI with 3 queries. Default example runner fails before invocation: undefined test_company fixture binding. Preserve both original inline example tables/all6rows, all original fixture recipes and independently authored expectations. No manual fixture replacements or app rewrites.
state.verified_implementation: IR builds exact fixture dependency closure from checked declarations, but foreign fixtures are excluded from local suite.fixtures and emitted as exampleImports tuples {provider,member,alias}. Currently alias uses declaration local name and can lose source alias; recipe dependencies similarly use declaration local names. Verified ir.rs decode_name_ref uses local_name(SymbolId) for s slots, and recipe/table dependency lists likewise use declaration local names. Thus different owners with the same local fixture name already collide; source aliases resolve to the declaration SymbolId but are not preserved as separate identity. Testkit rawNames indexes each raw recipe by one key, so multiple aliases of the same object in its fixtures map can also cause duplicate/wrong provisioning. These are concrete additional gaps; the initial exploratory requests misstated callback alias behavior and are superseded by this corrected state. BDD emits local fixture variables and direct references to dependency variables, but never binds imported ones. Runner/Testkit does not consume exampleImports, supplies imported={} by default. Provider fixture-only suites exist only if no local operation suite claims that fixture, and those orphan suites currently omit imported dependencies. Existing BDD same-module closure completion/topological ordering and Testkit dependency graph/provisioning are implemented.
state.accepted_semantics_and_draft: DESIGN requires imported aliases of the same fixture declaration to reuse its identity in isolated row, distinct declarations remain distinct, transitive dependencies provision before consumers once, user roles retain canonical owners, no production authority from fixture imports. DESIGN1279 proposes JS exampleFixtures({self,other,imported}) plus exampleImports canonical tuples; imported supplies recipes in same test context. This output convention is proposed/incomplete, not a proven implementation or language-level requirement to preserve a broken backend layout.
state.option_link: Complete canonical import linking with one internal key provider.member per fixture declaration, for ALL compiler-generated fixture scope slots/dependency keys; source aliases resolve to that key through checked SymbolId. Emit recipe-only provider modules for declarations that must be linked, including a locally claimed fixture used transitively through imports; operation suites consume the same canonical cached recipe object when that declaration is also a provider. A uniform provider per used declaration is acceptable only if it reduces the complete mechanism, not for symmetry. Existing {provider,member,alias} tuple remains, with canonical internal alias key; no extra runtime alias namespace. Loader resolves emitted canonical providers, caches one recipe object per declaration per test context, passes linked dependencies to factory, refuses missing/cyclic/conflicting graphs before setup. Existing fixture engine sees one provisioning entry per declaration. Compiler changes s keys and dependency strings; receiving graph logic and provider publication remain necessary. Avoids provider lexical wrappers and generated recipe duplication across suites; adds runtime linking and perhaps more small test modules.
state.option_flatten: Instead complete fixture closure at compile time into each suite using canonical declaration keys, preserving lexical source aliases through checked name rewriting or per-owner lexical recipe factories. Emit dependencies topologically once per canonical declaration within the suite and use the existing fixture engine without a runtime import resolver. This can remove one incomplete cross-module linking mechanism, but duplicates generated recipes across suites and requires robust owner-qualified symbol/alias/callback rewriting; accidental local-name collapse or distinct recipe identity per alias is unacceptable. Update proposed JS convention only if this total design is better, not merely because current code is broken.
state.comparison: Compare both on exactly the same original workflow and renamed/aliased multi-package reuse, diamond dependencies, same local fixture names in different owners, canonical user-role identity, setup versus business failure distinction, original source order and per-row isolation. Do not assume less code, existing machinery, draft spelling or fewer diagnostics is inherently superior. No broad new test architecture, new language syntax, user author boilerplate or deferred permission requirements. Select investigate if concrete unknowns prevent a justified bounded choice.
